subtopic: A promotion and the ego that follows
passage:
Mentor's notebook. Written by Mohit.
Met Sudha for our monthly coffee today. She was promoted to operations lead two months ago, and she's doing well: costs down, the delivery backlog cleared.
But I noticed it in the quarterly review last week and again today. 'I cut the costs.' 'I fixed the backlog.' 'I renegotiated the courier deal.' Every win, I. At the review, two people from her team glanced at each other when she said it. I don't think she saw.
I know that glow. I had it too, the year I was promoted.
Today, walking back to the car, I said quietly, 'Can I tell you something as a friend? Your team is noticing the "I". The backlog was Neeraj and Shobha as much as you.'
She stopped. Her face went tight for a second. Then she said, 'Oh. Oh no. You're right.' She thanked me before she got in the car.

qa.q: What was Sudha promoted to two months ago?
qa.a: She was promoted to operations lead two months ago.

qa.q: How did Sudha feel when Mohit mentioned the 'I', and how can you tell?
qa.a: She was stung at first, as her face went tight, and then embarrassed and grateful as she realised it was true.

qa.q: Why did Mohit's remark work, and what made the timing and place right?
qa.a: It was private, kind and specific, naming Neeraj and Shobha, so Sudha could hear it without losing face in front of her team.

qa.q: How might Neeraj and Shobha feel if Sudha starts crediting them by name?
qa.a: They are likely to feel seen and more willing to keep giving their best to her team.

grounding: It shows a mentor who notices a newly promoted friend claiming team wins as her own and offers a private, kind remark that the team has noticed.

subtopic: A promotion and the ego that follows
passage:
Saturday
Aadhya called tonight, happy, to tell me about the client presentation. It went well. I'm glad. But I counted, somewhere in the middle: 'my strategy', 'my deck', 'I closed it', 'I told them'. Maybe fourteen times. Her team of five did most of that deck. I know, because Leena was up till two on it and texted me.
Two months ago Aadhya was the person who always said 'we'. The promotion's changed something.
I almost said nothing. It isn't my business, and she's so happy.
But I remember what happened to Suresh in my old office. His team simply stopped trying, and nobody told him why until it was too late.
So at the end of the call I said, 'Can I say one small thing, as your friend? Your team might be hearing a lot of "I" lately.'
She went quiet. Then: 'Yash. Seriously?' A pause. 'Okay. Tell me more.'

qa.q: How many people are on Aadhya's team?
What was Yash worried about before deciding to speak up?
qa.a: Yash worried it wasn't Yash's business and might spoil Aadhya's happiness, but feared her team would stop trying, like Suresh's did.

qa.q: What made Yash's remark a good way to raise the problem?
qa.a: It was private, framed as coming from a friend, and short, which let Aadhya ask for more instead of feeling attacked.

qa.q: How might Leena feel if Aadhya starts saying 'we' again about the deck?
qa.a: Leena would likely feel her late nights were noticed and valued, and trust Aadhya more.

grounding: It shows a friend noticing a newly promoted person speaking in the first person about team wins and choosing to mention it privately and kindly.
